target.title: fix(openrouter): apply request policy to video catalog requests
target.body:
## Summary
- OpenRouter video catalog discovery and per-model capability resolution now pass configured provider request overrides into `resolveProviderHttpRequestConfig` instead of silently ignoring `models.providers.openrouter.request`.
- The catalog fetch now uses resolved request headers and private-network policy while preserving OpenRouter's API-key authorization and attribution headers.
- The live catalog cache key now includes a stable sanitized request-policy discriminator, so one baseUrl/API key cannot reuse catalog results fetched with different request headers or private-network settings.

## Verification
- `TMPDIR=/media/vdc/0668001470/tmp/openclaw-task-tmp node scripts/run-vitest.mjs extensions/openrouter/video-generation-provider.test.ts` - passed; `Test Files  1 passed (1)`, `Tests  19 passed (19)`.
- `TMPDIR=/media/vdc/0668001470/tmp/openclaw-task-tmp node scripts/run-oxlint.mjs --tsconfig config/tsconfig/oxlint.extensions.json extensions/openrouter/video-model-catalog.ts extensions/openrouter/video-generation-provider.test.ts` - passed; exit 0.
- `git diff --check` - passed; exit 0.
- Mutation check A: temporarily removing the catalog `request:` plumbing made focused Vitest fail because the expected configured request overrides were `undefined`; restoring the patch returned the test to green.
- Mutation check B: temporarily removing `params.requestPolicyCacheKey` from the catalog cache key made `keys live OpenRouter video catalog cache by request policy` fail with `expected "vi.fn()" to be called 2 times, but got 1 times`; restoring the patch returned the test to green.

## Real behavior proof

Behavior addressed: OpenRouter video catalog HTTP requests now honor configured provider request overrides, and the live catalog cache no longer reuses a result fetched under a different request policy.

Real environment tested: local Linux Node source checkout using a real `node:http` server on `127.0.0.1` and the exported `listOpenRouterVideoModelCatalog` runtime path. The only external service was the local HTTP server; no third-party OpenRouter traffic was sent. The fake API key was redacted in output.

Exact command run after this patch: `node --import tsx --input-type=module` with an inline script that starts a local catalog endpoint, calls `listOpenRouterVideoModelCatalog` twice against the same baseUrl/API key with different `models.providers.openrouter.request.headers`, and prints what the server actually received.

Evidence after fix:

```text
openrouter-video-catalog-request-policy-proof
server_requests=2
first_model=local/veo-policy-1
second_model=local/veo-policy-2
received_policies=policy-a,policy-b
received_auth=Bearer ***,Bearer ***
```

Observed result after fix: the local server received two real HTTP GETs for the same baseUrl/API key and saw the two different configured request-policy headers. Without the cache-key fix, the second call is served from the first cached catalog result and the regression test observes only one outbound fetch.

What was not tested: a live OpenRouter production endpoint was not called; this proof validates the OpenClaw request-policy and cache behavior without sending third-party network traffic.
